decisions.rationale: Impaired glucose tolerance is a single defined metabolic condition (a prediabetic state identified by a specific glucose tolerance test), not a family of diseases, so it is a Specific Disease mention in the title.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 - Specific Disease; Examples 2 and 6

decisions.rationale: Same defined condition as candidate 1, mentioned again in the abstract; duplicate mentions within the text are annotated separately.

decisions.rationale: IGT is the standard abbreviation of impaired glucose tolerance. The long form and the abbreviation are separate synonymous mentions, so the abbreviation is annotated as its own Specific Disease mention.

decisions.rationale: Hypertriglyceridemia is a specific, defined lipid disorder (elevated plasma triglycerides) rather than a general term, so it is a Specific Disease mention.

decisions.rationale: Diabetes mellitus is a family of multiple specific diseases (type 1, type 2, and other forms) rather than one definable disease, so it is a Disease Class mention.

Cardiovascular disease is a broad category covering many specific conditions (e.g., coronary artery disease, stroke), analogous to the autosomal recessive disease example, so it is a Disease Class mention.

decisions.rationale: Hyperglycerolemia is a specific, defined biochemical disorder (plasma glycerol above a stated threshold), not a general term or a process, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease mention with the minimal span.
